title: The Glorious Revolution 1688
welcome_lead: James II, William of Orange and the constitutional settlement that bound the crown to Parliament.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on 1688, the Bill of Rights and constitutional monarchy.
final_note: You have witnessed a bloodless transfer of sovereignty.

walkthroughs.body_html: James II promoted Catholics in the army, universities and government, defying Anglican opinion. His 1687 Declaration of Indulgence and prosecution of the Seven Bishops in June 1688 alienated the establishment. The birth of a Catholic heir on 10 June 1688 ended hopes of a Protestant succession. The Immortal Seven invited William on 30 June.

William landed at Torbay on 5 November 1688 with 15,000 troops. Lacking support, James fled to France in December. A Convention Parliament met in January 1689 and declared the throne vacant, offering it jointly to William and Mary alongside the Declaration of Rights, later enacted as the Bill of Rights. Sovereignty now rested on parliamentary contract.

The 1689 Bill of Rights banned standing armies without consent, secured free elections and parliamentary privilege. The 1689 Toleration Act allowed Dissenter worship. Annual Mutiny Acts and the 1694 Triennial Act forced regular Parliaments. The 1701 Act of Settlement excluded Catholics from succession. Together these acts created a constitutional monarchy.
